primitives.verbatim_quote: It has been written on the assumption that all behavior, individual and social, moral and immoral, normal and psychopathic, is generated from the same primary laws; that the differences in the objective behavioral manifestations are due to the differing conditions under which habits are set up and function.

reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational premise of Hull's work posits that all forms of behavior—whether individual, social, moral, or pathological—are generated by identical underlying laws. This implies a universal framework for modeling behavior, which can be formalized as a set of molar principles. These principles operate within a shared mathematical structure, enabling cross-domain applicability. The derivation proceeds from the assumption of law invariance to construct a kernel-based model of habitual behavior, where each instance of behavior reflects a unique instantiation of the same generative mechanism. The failure mode occurs when environmental variability outpaces the capacity of habitual conditioning to adapt, leading to maladaptive or novel behaviors. Dualities emerge in how these principles manifest: one in the uniformity of origin, another in the diversity of expression. The mathematical representation is abstracted into symbolic operators that map inputs (stimuli) to outputs (responses), with probabilistic weights reflecting the strength of learned associations.
